watch.en: Cream butter and sugar at low to medium speed until white, light and fluffy.
watch.de: Butter und Zucker bei niedriger bis mittlerer Stufe schaumig rühren, bis die Masse weiß, hell und locker ist.

why.en: Low speed forms the best air cells for the texture of the cake; a high speed warms the mix.
why.de: Eine niedrige Stufe bildet die besten Luftzellen für die Textur des Kuchens; eine hohe Stufe erwärmt die Masse.

sources.title: Introduction to Baking and Pastries (Rink and Thibodeaux)
sources.place: chapter 1.7 Cake and Buttercreams, section Creaming Method
sources.sentence: You will cream them until they are white, light and fluffy.

sources.title: Introduction to Baking and Pastries (Rink and Thibodeaux)
sources.place: chapter 1.7 Cake and Buttercreams, section Texture of the Batter
sources.sentence: Butter and granulated sugar combinations at low speed create the best air cells for a good cake texture.

sources.title: Introduction to Baking and Pastries (Rink and Thibodeaux)
sources.place: chapter 1.7 Cake and Buttercreams, section Texture of the Batter
sources.sentence: Too high a speed will cause the mix to become warm and not allow for proper formation.

sources.title: McGee on Food and Cooking (Harold McGee), Hodder & Stoughton 2004
sources.place: chapter Cereal Doughs and Batters, p. 557
sources.sentence: Butter is best aerated at a relatively cool 65°F/18°C, while shortening creams most effectively at a warm room temperature, between 75 and 80°F/24-27°C.
